svg.text: 1. Blast pad, then a displaced threshold (landing toward the right)
Blast pad or stopway: yellow chevrons. No taxi, takeoff, or landing
Demarcation bar: 3 ft, yellow (it is not on the runway)
Displaced area: white arrows. Takeoff and rollout OK; no touchdown
White arrowheads across the runway just before the threshold bar
Threshold bar: 10 ft, white. The landing runway starts here
Threshold stripes and runway number follow
Closed for takeoff and landing in both directions; old paint may still show.
The other direction is shortened too. The NOTAM tells you (e.g., 9/27 W 900 CLSD).
3. Closed runway: yellow X at each end
Permanently closed: X at each end and every 1,000 ft. A lit yellow X may be
used instead, and some closures have none: check NOTAMs and ATIS.
